#133517 62 2006-01-18T23:14:15Z smartalco
several things to point out... mainly all responses to daddaluma's posts

the instant as you type searching is in the os, he's not talking about a google thing in safari, in tiger there is a little blue icon on the top right of the screen, click it (or theres a key command to make it pop up) and a little space appears to type in, the instant you start typing it looks for apps, folders, documents, pics, etc that have similar names to what your typing (if you start with a n lets say, it will start looking for anything that starts with a n), and if you hit apple-f, it will bring up a specialized search menu, cept you can customize to only search for certain types of files, the search results are neatly desplayed for you, and if you change on letter, it will revise its search instant, that is as you type searching

widgets are very helpful, they arent programs per say, but little parts of a larger program called dashboard that runs transparently, (as in always on), hit the right key (F8 on my laptop) and a semi-transparent film will cover your desktop and all your open widgets will appear, they range from customizable clocks, instant weather watcher, dictionary, phonebook, a movie listings finder, translator, unit converter (ie, mm to inches, basically any normal unit to any other), mini games (snake, tetris, minesweeper), theres even one that spits out random shakespear quotes, etc (there are over 1000 downlowdable ones at apple.com), once again, not huge, but very helpful

i must admit i havent really tried to do anything in automater so im out of that debate

safari has a pop-up blocker too, just hit apple-k to toggle it on and off, or go and click on it in some menu (forgot which one), i have yet to get one single pop-up with it on, and it still hasnt affected anything ive tried to do

all the iLife features come default when you buy a new comp, its just if you want to upgrade older versions that you have to buy it, and most of that stuff is really cool, especially for comming with the comp

viewing all windows is very helpful, and i cant say all windows will have probs, some are just fluks that happen to only some ppl, some depend on what you do with the comp, but at least you admitted a couple things on the mac are better, yay your on your way to seeing the light

i must admit, there are times when i want to see an alienware comp in the place of my mac, as long as its still running OSX, building your own can be fairly cool, you got me on just one point so far

#150471 65 2006-03-01T23:15:52Z smartalco
the location for the .sol file on a mac is as follows...

Macintosh HD (your hard drive) -> Users -> whatever the username is of the account your on (the one with the little house thing next to it) ->Library -> Preferences -> Macromedia -> Flashplayer -> #Shared Objects -> 3QNYZYNH ->localhost -> n_v14b_userdata.sol

if that fails just do a search, apple-f, if you dont have 10.4 (the os) then it will bring up a box and where it has a thing that says "name" in a pull down thing, chose extension, then type in sol with no . and that should get you there

The invisibility with radar only works against other radar systems. It doesn't make you unable to be seen or anything. Radar systems are extremely simple compared to the human eye, so distorting radar and distorting visible light are two very, very different things. im to lazy to read the articles but ray tracing in general refers to when you render a 3d model the computer sends out "rays" of light from all light sources in the scene, these rays then bounce off the objects and using algorithms the color/intensity/angle of the reflected/refracted ray is calculated and continues on its path until it either ends up completely leaving the scene or makes its way into the camera position of the scene... hope that helps

Quote
Q: How BIG is this page?

A: This page is 9 quadrillion pixels wide by 9 quadrillion pixels tall. Thus it contains a large number of pixels:
8,100,000,000,000,000,000,000,000,000,000

otherwise known as 8.1 nonillion. In scientific notation, that's 8.1x10^30, hereafter shown in the form 8.1e30.

This means that the repeating background image has 5.4e28 stars on it-- about as many as there would be if our universe was multiplied to a million times it's current observable size.

Futhermore, at 77 pixels to the inch, this page takes up 3.4e18 square miles and is 1.844 billion miles on a side-- an area roughly equivalent to a section of the plane of our Solar System with the sun at the center and the orbit of Saturn on the outside edge (a square 22 AU on a side). That's about 17 billion times the surface area of the Earth.

Test it for yourself. Using the arrow keys to scroll, see if you can move the scroll button even one pixel. On second thought, don't-- especially if you're the doggedly persistent type. To do so will take about seven times longer than your natural lifespan. This method causes you to "move" across the plane of this page at the equivalent of a toddler's walking pace-- around 0.5 mph. At this rate, it would take you half a million years to cross from one end to the other.

As you may know, it is enormously quicker to use the mouse and click on the empty part of the scroll bar and then hold down the mouse button. Using this method, you would be able to cross in about 100 minutes. Doing so causes you to move at about Warp 1.5-- a virtual velocity of over 1.5 times the speed of light (ignoring relativistic effects). If you try it, you'll see that the background starfield appears to be going by at no more than ten miles an hour. In actuality, the glimpses you are seeing of the starfield are tens of thousands of miles apart. Enormous expanses are being skipped over completely.

Of course, it is far quicker to use the mouse to grab the scroll button and slide it over. Not as quick as using this link, however: To the Corner.

Click here for another angle on how big this page is.

Note: While this page is very, very large when viewed using Internet Explorer and others, you need Mozilla Firefox to view it properly. Firefox is the open-source phoenix of once-defeated Netscape. It offers improved speed, security, and simplicity. It's tabs feature alone makes it worth switching. It's free.
Quote
Here's another way to imagine the size of this webpage.

Let us exaggerate outrageously and say that a trillion books might have been written during the history of the world (a figure more in line with all reading that has ever been done), and that each of those trillion books has an extremely generous allotment of 10,000 pages. Let us then say that each of those pages has an average size of about one square foot. That would mean that this webpage would have ten trillion times the space necessary to fit it all in.

If you were to do a random search of this webpage at a rate of ten pageviews per second, it would take you about 31,000 years-- on average-- before you would find even a single page of even one of those books.
And here's another way to look at it.
Quote
The World Wide Web is currently the biggest part of the internet-- and it is huge.
Google currently knows of over 8 billion webpages-- and there are certainly a great many pages that Google does not know about. There are an unknowable number that have come and gone and will never be seen again.

Let us imagine that there have been a total of a twenty billion webpages each year since 1990-- a gross overestimation (at least in regard to the early days).

Let us then imagine that each of those webpages was at least 25,000 pixels long and 1,000 pixels wide-- equivalent to about twenty-five pages of writing.

Given these figures, this one page would have enough raw area to house a quadrillion years worth of the World Wide Web.

If you were to search randomly at a rate of ten pageviews per second, it would take you 3 million years-- on average-- to find even just one of those twenty billion pages.

#214832 17 2006-08-12T22:26:03Z smartalco
no, not really, when someone makes a program, its normally not one guy making a progam, its many (least for bigger programs), that are all linked together when compiled, thats just one reason many programs are in multiple files, for games your gonna have all the images that are shown throughout the game as seperate files (least most of the time), and for progams that can or do use more then one window (basically all) will probably have some program file that manages the window size and look upon opening a new one, and headers that you need for the one program will be different files, and you can put different functions in different files if you want... and i could go on

for an example go to the developer folder (im assuming you have installed xcode), then Examples, then AppKit, then TextEdit, then open the TextEdit.xcode (it will ask you to uprade a copy, just name it TextEdit.xcodeproj) and look at all the files in there just for something like text edit, it's amazing how much goes into something little like that

In Toronto, Metanet Software received funding to extend its 2D freeware adventure/puzzle game N to Microsoft's Xbox Live Arcade under the new title N+. The new version will add better graphics and multiplayer modes and should be released in November.

President Mare Sheppard says the new media fund at Telefilm Canada allows indie developers to make titles for mainstream consoles, which would otherwise be prohibitively expensive. A development kit for the Xbox 360 runs upwards of $10,000, for instance.

"As independent, small developers, we can develop pretty easily for PC, Mac, Linux. But getting to the consoles and systems outside of that is much more difficult if you don't have any funding," says Sheppard.

why? because im right!!!, i can garuntee you havent looked into this as much as i have, all macs use .app files, period, and they are indeed in the same format, the term for the applications that can run on powerpc and intel chips under osx are know as "universal binaries" in apples terms, all of apples apps are universal, meaning the itunes im running on my powerbook (powerpc chip) and the itunes that someone else is running on their macbook (intel chip) is exactly the same!, all of it!, and if you have an app that was ment for powerpc and the developer hasnt released an universal binary of it (photoshop is a good example) then you can still run it on an intel mac, apple also integrated a thing called rosetta into the intel version of OSX, it can take the application ment for powerpc and translate the code during runtime into x86 code, hardly slowing down the process at all, and you still cant run .exe's on intel macs without emulation, period, so yes, indeed, as you said at the end, you can drag and drop the same .app file between a powerpc mac and a intel mac and it will work both ways, so please, stop argueing of which you apparently know nothing about

A pack consisting of 100 levels, but not by one person, or two, or three, but by 100 people, a pack comprised of the best map of each author arranged (hopefully) into episodic fashion (although not necessary, thats up to you people).

Group episodes (5 maps) may be submitted by a group of 5 people, but each person that participated in making that episode will not be allowed to submit another map.

#15937 1 2007-06-27T19:53:14Z smartalco
For those of you who don't know (probably most of you), I live in Kansas and my family farms. (the reason for my recent absence that none of you noticed)

To have a little revenge on the people that assume people in Kansas don't have access to the internet (someone has actually asked me on a forum 'Do you have the internet in kansas?', my response: 'No, and neither do you, but I do have access to the internet.') I am going to assume the majority of you know nothing of farming, so, into a brief explanation of the terms I will then use to portray the approximate size of our little operation.

/*you can skip this section if you just want to see the pictures*/

quarter - 1/2 mile x 1/2 mile (hence the name, its one quarter of a square mile)
acre - 43560 sq ft., to give it a little perspective, its 1/2 mile x 16.5 feet
bushel - a volume measurement mainly used for grain, one bushel is apprx. 8 (dry) gallons
combine - the largest of the big green things with an engine your going to see, named that because it combined 2 functions that used to be done by different machines, cutting, and thrashing
tractor - smaller of the green things with an engine, basically just pulls stuff, lots of really heavy stuff

my family owns 7 quarters, although only 4 of them are entirely planted, 2 of the have grazing ground for our cattle, and the last just has some terrain that can't be planted, and we had 475 acres planted this year

on an average year an acre will yield 35-40 bushels of grain, this year we averaged about 30, some higher some lower

now, on to the pictures!


some wheat!, very exciting stuff here



a before and after in pretty much the exact same spot



a couple of our combine



this is what I drive (all the important controls (shift, throttle, hydraulics) are right at your fingertips, as is shown)



these two were taken within about 15 seconds of each other, thats my dad driving the combine while cutting wheat and unloading the already cut grain into the grain cart that is attached to the tractor that im driving while taking these pictures o_O (these were kinda difficult to take, it was on a curvy terrace too >_>)

So, uh... discuss or ask questions or something!

i use a key listener for keys that you would press and not hold, and onClipEvent to detect if keys are pressed upon entering the frame

key listener:
myListener = new Object();
myListener.onKeyDown = function () {
	if(Key.isDown(80)){
  /*code to be executed when specified key is pressed*/
	}
}
myListener.onKeyUp = function () {
	
}

Key.addListener(myListener);
}

just replace the number 80 with the corresponding key code (i forgot where i found these, you will have to do some searching

onClipEvent:
onClipEvent(enterFrame) {
	if(Key.isDown(key.RIGHT)) {
               /*code to be executed*/
        }
}

just replace key.RIGHT with the key you want

i would start with processing (www.processing.org), its java based, which means you will learn all the standard programming features (if/else, switch, loops, etc), yet it makes it very simple to actually output something graphically to the screen, which is very cool

after that, if you want to get a little more experience, do python

and finally go into C or C++, which you should be able to pick up the basis of pretty quick because just about all programming languages are the same at their base, just with a little different syntax, its when you get to the complicated stuff that they differ

i would avoid java, its like C, except slow, and /slightly/ easier to learn

as far as your first little problem there, a browser always tries to go to the index (index.html, index.php, etc) page of the folder if a specific file isn't specified in the url (in this case the 'sub.htm' part of the url), so to just have the url be 'www.homeworkhlp.org' you need to rename your 'sub.htm' page to 'index.html' (yes, .html, don't use .htm)

Did you read the wiki entry at all?
It's a highly compressed format meant to be read and executed, not split apart.
It's not a custom game format; it was made by Apple to generally prevent what you're trying to do. Not much is known about the format, so thusly, there isn't a solid way to make an extractor for it.

yes, specifically the part where it says it is a format intended to be opened by the Installer in OS X (the program is called 'Installer'), it isn't a Windows format

anyone can make any combination of letters an extension for a file their program needs, I could make a text editor that saves its files with .exe, it would be really dumb, but it is possible

the only thing that is going on here, is whoever developed that game decided to put some of its resources in a file that happens to use .pkg as an extension, it has nothing to do with Apple's format, and there probably isn't any program on earth that can correctly open it (aside from the game itself, opening it when it needs to)

SUPER EDIT: I have been ignoring this thread, because I am tired of OS wars (everwhere, not just here), so here is me weighing in on some crap

@Strife: about your friends preferring OS X, it would probably be because of the underlying unix part, thousands of scientific tools become available (just a guess)

@Tapp: *facepalm* you have no idea what you are talking about, go away, please

I have never emulated Windows on my mac (nor do I have a windows computer), and I don't expect to ever need to (however, going into Comp. Sci. this fall at KU, I am building a computer, which will obviously run windows, since the major pretty much requires it, it will be hackintoshed though ), the only thing I have ever found that OS X is lacking to Windows is support for games I want, and that is slowly changing (if Valve would just port the Source engine I'd be set...), everything else, yes everything that I have used on Windows I have been able to find an equivalent or better program on OS X

I will admit, part of my liking of OS X comes from a decade of using it, and knowing the ins and outs of OS X, and I know where to look for new software (there is a quite large OS X development community, the resources and groups are just harder to find, given the 6% US marketshare), and quite a few linux apps can be run via X11, since they require very minimal modification to get working under X11 from the original build (GIMP is one such obvious app, the normal dev branch doesn't have an OS X build, but some random guy took the source, made a few changes, and has an X11/OS X release for every normal GIMP release)

My sister has a older MacBook with specs of 1.8ghz Core Duo, 512mb RAM, and of course integrated graphics (this was bought fairly early in the intel switch, and it was the cheapest one), it runs OS X 10.5 (the newest release) quite nearly as fast as my parents Powerbook w/ 2.2ghz C2D, 2gb RAM, and some form of a dedicated graphics card, try running Vista on 512 ram and integrated graphics and you will have time to get a soda opening the C:/ drive (despite this being somewhat of an exaggeration, I have used Vista on a laptop w/ 512 ram and integrated graphics, and that thing is acts as if it is trying to render Crysis style graphics full time), OS X is just a much lighter OS (I have found it to be in line with XP performance)

*thinks for a moment about where I was going with my rambling... probably no where, continues rambling*

about all OS X programs looking the same: So? I find that to be a good thing. I don't want to spend the time learning 17 different GUI's that I will use daily. With OS X, similar functions have the same commands across nearly any set of programs, Cmd-, (thats command-comma, the comma isn't part of the sentence) is universally the apps preference pane, Cmd-Q quits the program, Cmd-W closes the window, Cmd-M minimizes the current window, and there are countless other examples!, rather then learn a new set of commands for every different program, I just have to know a basic set common to all and the few unique ones to each program, I can download a program I have never used before, and know that Cmd-, will bring up the preference pane (and for the record: OS X doesn't lock you in to these commands, they are all customizable, but because Apple defined these behaviors in their own programs developed in house, and kept them consistent across all these programs, everyone else uses them to, it just helps the usability of the OS)(also: it is possible to customize the GUI as well, but no one does it for the same reasons outlined above (and it is ridiculously easy to make standard GUI features with Apple's dev tools), Adobe AIR will never take off on OS X because it breaks the standards of the OS, the standards that work and work well)

which leads me to another thing, Apple has a phenomenal set of dev tools available entirely for free, I use the same tools as Apple devs themselves when I do my fiddling in programming, with M$ there are a bazillion levels of the dev tools you can get, the best ones cost a few thousand, and the Apple dev tools are quite awesome, everything you do (aside from the actual type-in-the-code part) has several ways to be done, via key-commands, menu items, or gui ways, when connecting a class to a GUI text field, you just ctrl-click then drag from the class to the text field in the interface builder (note: this might mean nothing to those who don't use Obj-C/Cocoa)(for an overview of the advantages of Apple's dev tools and related stuff, I link you here, the conversion articles are pretty good, unfortunately #4 hasn't been released yet...(and the guy who wrote those used to be a diehard Windows user))

one thing up there that I mentioned drives me nuts with M$, their OS pricing scheme, give me the whole dam OS, not parts of it, you have to pay nearly $300 to get the whole OS! I can get a family pack of OS X with 5 licenses for $200! as many as MS sells, there is no reason to charge $300 for an OS (I'm aware you can get Home Basic for 1/3 of that, but then your not getting all the stuff)

I'm done rambling for now *listens to the collective sigh of relief*, I'll continue to watch this thread and only post when I see some glaringly obvious fallacies, so, if you don't want to see me again, don't say anything ridiculously stupid

@T3chno: I don't suggest to anyone that they should switch, I'm saying try it for a few weeks (obviously you aren't going to buy a mac to try it, but borrow a friends or something, you could even trade computers, they can 'try' windows for a couple weeks and you can try OS X)

starting with my freshman year, my high school did what they called a '1 to 1 laptop initiative', basically, every student gets a laptop to carry around/take home/use in class for the duration of the school year (mid august through mid may), the first lease was 3 years, on some iBook G4's, when the news broke out I was probably one of 10 people happy about it, at the end of the year they had a poll on our high school website, 80% of the students said they now preferred macs over PCs

since it was a 3 year lease, they asked the various companies to bid on the next lease between my junior and senior year, Dell ended up with a cheaper bid then Apple by $10,000 (this is on a $960k lease, not exactly a big difference between $960,000 and $970,000), so the school board, being entirely uniformed on the situation and going with what was (slightly) cheaper only, and ignoring the request of the students (and teachers), they went with Dell, at the end of my senior year they had another poll: 90% still preferred macs over PC's after using the Dell Latitudes for 9 months

just food for thought

#20738 1 2008-07-07T17:32:10Z smartalco
HARVEST REPORT 2008
*Eagle Cry*
*pronounced 'Harvess Repore 2008'*

(Last years thread here if you wish to see it, since I'm lazy, most of the following is copied straight out of it)

For those of you who don't know (probably most of you), I live in Kansas and my family farms. (the reason for my recent absence that none of you noticed)

To have a little revenge on the people that assume people in Kansas don't have access to the internet (someone has actually asked me on a forum 'Do you have the internet in kansas?', my response: 'No, and neither do you, but I do have access to the internet.') I am going to assume the majority of you know nothing of farming, so, into a brief explanation of the terms I will then use to portray the approximate size of our little operation.

/*you can skip this section if you just want to see the pictures*/

quarter - 1/2 mile x 1/2 mile (hence the name, its one quarter of a square mile)
acre - 43560 sq ft., to give it a little perspective, its 1/2 mile x 16.5 feet (or if my calculations are correct, ~4/5 of a (american) football field)
bushel - a volume measurement mainly used for grain, one bushel is apprx. 8 (dry) gallons (also, 60 some odd pounds)
combine - the largest of the big green things with an engine your going to see, named that because it combined 2 functions that used to be done by different machines, cutting, and thrashing
tractor - smaller of the green things with an engine, basically just pulls stuff, lots of really heavy stuff, like a grain cart loaded with ~24,000 lbs. of wheat (thats 24 thousand pounds, 12 tons, 10,886 kg)

overall our year was very good, we harvest over 3x the amount of wheat we did 2 years ago, on the same amount of land

have any questions about things? ask away!
